lenses.question: Are the quantities in this part dimensionally closed (l_g, r_*, SI)? What unit does each symbol carry? Is the x/u identification valid without an explicit length scale?
What are the u->0 and u->infinity limits in this part — converge/diverge/saturate? Is the asymptotic form consistent across parts?
Which u/rho domain does this part operate in — overlapping or disjoint? Physical phase or coordinate convention?
For each constant/relation in this part: input, measurement, declaration, inheritance, rescaling, or fit? Cite file:line.
What is the measurement chain, instrument, proxy, nuisance, and calibration for this part? Measured or declared?
Is the object in this part IDENTICAL in MOND/LCDM/EFC, or an interpretation difference via coordinate/measure/instrument/proxy/regime/phase? State the exact axis of difference.
What is the covariant form of this part, and does it reduce to the discrete/non-relativistic form? Which signs, normalizations, time-scalings are carried?
Can a blind user reproduce the number/relation in this part from source alone? What is the minimal runnable proof and its file:line?

rules: Every lens must produce a verdict for EVERY one of the 6 parts — even parts far from its home. A part it cannot judge is 'unknown' (with reason), never silently skipped.
'not_applicable' is FORBIDDEN without an explicit one-line reason in not_applicable_reason. In a rotation most lenses apply to most parts; default to 'open'/'unknown' when thin.

For EVERY part, additionally answer the paradigm/coordinate question (identical across MOND/LCDM/EFC, or a coordinate/measure/instrument/proxy/regime/phase difference?). This is the holistic test and must not be skipped even though it is 'the paradigm lens's' domain.
Every non-empty finding carries file:line evidence. No evidence -> 'open', never 'satisfied'.
Attack the established points: where the source actually contradicts the established v3.1 reading, say so. Same-model agreement is reading-consistency, not validation.
Do NOT write to repo files. Output returns as JSON.
Cell status vocabulary: satisfied / open / unknown / contradicted / not_applicable.
